pointers.sentence: With `"pool"` in an alias's `"OPTIONS"`, `True` or the pool's arguments, the backend's `pool` property makes one pool for the process, and each connection is taken from it as it opens (`django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.pool`, `django/db/backends/oracle/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.pool`).

With `"pool"` in an alias's `"OPTIONS"`, `True` or the pool's arguments, the backend's `pool` property makes one pool for the process, and each connection is taken from it as it opens (`django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.pool`, `django/db/backends/oracle/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.pool`).

The release notes' reason: opening a connection can take relatively long, and keeping connections open can reduce latency (`docs/releases/5.1.txt`; [Opening and closing a connection](../backends/lifecycle.md#connection-pools-postgresql-and-oracle)).
Since 5.1 SQLite's backend takes two keys out of `"OPTIONS"` before the rest reach `sqlite3.connect` (`django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.get_connection_params`).
`"init_command"` is split at each semicolon, each command run on every new connection after Django's two pragmas (`django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.get_new_connection`).

`"transaction_mode"`, `"DEFERRED"`, `"EXCLUSIVE"` or `"IMMEDIATE"`, capitals or not, is written after the `"BEGIN"` that opens an outermost atomic block, and any other string raises `ImproperlyConfigured` (`django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py:DatabaseWrapper._start_transaction_under_autocommit`; [SQLite](../backends/sqlite.md#opening-a-connection-get_connection_params-and-get_new_connection)).

Since 5.2 MySQL's backend asks for the character set `"utf8mb4"`, where it asked for `"utf8"`, which the release notes call an alias of the deprecated `"utf8mb3"`; a `"charset"` in `"OPTIONS"` still wins (`django/db/backends/mysql/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.get_connection_params`; [MySQL and MariaDB](../backends/mysql.md#the-driver-mysqldb-and-opening-a-connection)).
Since 5.0 a `UUIDField` on MariaDB is a column of the database's type `"uuid"`, where it was `"char(32)"`, as it still is on MySQL (`django/db/backends/mysql/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.data_types`).
The release notes say MariaDB 10.7 and later; at this commit the flag is whether the server is MariaDB at all (`django/db/backends/mysql/features.py:DatabaseFeatures.has_native_uuid_field`).

The field writes a `uuid.UUID` for a native column and its hex otherwise (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:UUIDField.get_db_prep_value`), so a `"char(32)"` column an earlier release made on MariaDB no longer matches ([Column types: from a field to a column](../backends/column-types.md#mysqls-two-properties)).

Since 5.0 SQLite's operations object gives every integer field a 64-bit range, from 0 for the positive ones, its comment saying that sqlite3 supports integers up to 64 bits (`django/db/backends/sqlite3/operations.py:DatabaseOperations.integer_field_range`).

At this commit `django/db/backends/oracle/base.py` imports `oracledb` alone, and raises `ImproperlyConfigured` where it cannot ([Oracle](../backends/oracle.md#the-driver-and-the-processs-environment)).

Since 6.1 `django.db.transaction.savepoint` warns with `RemovedInDjango2028Warning` and calls `savepoint_create` (`django/db/transaction.py:savepoint`; [Transactions: autocommit, `atomic` and savepoints](../backends/transactions.md#savepoints); [What still warns: the deprecations and the releases that end them](deprecations.md)).

Since 5.0 a function under `functools.cache` or `functools.lru_cache` is written by name: on CPython it is an instance of `functools._lru_cache_wrapper`, which the serializer adds to `FUNCTION_TYPES` (`django/db/migrations/serializer.py:FUNCTION_TYPES`).

Since 6.0 `ZoneInfoSerializer` writes a `zoneinfo.ZoneInfo`, and keyword arguments of a deconstructed call whose names are not identifiers go into a dictionary after `**` (`django/db/migrations/serializer.py:DeconstructibleSerializer.serialize_deconstructed`).

Since 5.1 an operation has a **category**, `Operation.category`, a member of `OperationCategory`, whose values are signs: `"+"` an addition, `"-"` a removal, `"~"` an alteration, `"p"` Python, `"s"` SQL, `"?"` a mix. makemigrations prints `Operation.formatted_description`, sign and description, for each operation it writes or merges; a category of `None`, the base class's, shows `"?"` (`django/db/migrations/operations/base.py:Operation.formatted_description`; [Operations: the base class and its two halves](../migrations/operations.md#category-describe-and-the-name-fragment)).

Since 5.2 a constraint changed only in the attributes `BaseConstraint.non_db_attrs` lists, `violation_error_message` and `violation_error_code`, becomes an `AlterConstraint`, which changes the project state and sends nothing; a constraint changed otherwise is still removed and added, in the database too, except where a field it names was renamed and kept its db_column (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._constraint_should_be_dropped_and_recreated`; [The autodetector: fields, indexes and constraints](../migrations/autodetector-fields.md#constraints-create_altered_constraints)).

`MigrationAutodetector._detect_changes` sorts an unmanaged model with the others (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._detect_changes`); its operations change the state and no table, since `Operation.allow_migrate_model` refuses a model whose options say it cannot be migrated (`django/db/migrations/operations/base.py:Operation.allow_migrate_model`), and the questioner is asked no default for a field it gains that cannot be null ([The autodetector: comparing two project states](../migrations/autodetector.md#detect_changes-the-models-sorted-then-the-generators-in-order)).
